sections.html:
Madison is a city in Madison County that reaches west into Limestone County, with Huntsville on every side of it. It sits in the Huntsville metro area about 11 miles west of downtown Huntsville, covers 30.694 square miles at roughly 686 feet, and uses ZIP codes 35756, 35757 and 35758. Small unincorporated pockets remain inside and along the border, so a Madison mailing address does not always mean a Madison city address.

The 2020 census counted 56,933 residents, up from 14,904 in 1990, and the 2025 estimate is 67,968. There were 21,980 housing units with 5.4 percent vacant and 20,787 households, and 41.1 percent of households had children under 18. Homeowner vacancy was 1.0 percent and rental vacancy 8.6 percent, so few owner-occupied homes sit empty.

Much of the housing is recent. That usually means fewer major system failures, but also many similar houses on the market at once, so a house that needs work competes with many move-in-ready ones nearby.

Many residents commute to Cummings Research Park and Redstone Arsenal in Huntsville, about 12 miles away. The regional economy is aerospace and defense, and a job change in that sector can mean a sudden move for a Madison family.

Madison City Schools, formed in 1998, serves more than 13,300 students from the city and the town of Triana, with several elementary schools, three middle schools and two high schools, Bob Jones and James Clemens. Families often shop by school zone, so expect buyers to ask which campuses your house feeds.

Interstate 565, U.S. 72 (University Drive) and Madison Boulevard (State Route 20) carry traffic east and west, and Slaughter Road, Hughes Road, Wall Triana Highway and County Line Road run north and south. A Norfolk Southern main line runs through town, which matters for houses close to the tracks. TRAM provides dial-a-ride transit for Madison County.

Madison has greenways and parks, including Palmer Park, and is working with Huntsville and Decatur on a 70-mile bicycling and walking trail called the Singing River Trail. Buyers who commute to Research Park often value those amenities along with the schools, so mention nearby parks and trail access in your description.

Inside the city of Madison the Madison County tax rate is $6.95 per $100 of assessed value. Taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, and after that a $5 late fee and 1 percent monthly interest apply. The county also holds an online tax lien sale each May.

A satellite office at 100 Plaza Blvd in Madison takes payments weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Part of Madison lies in Limestone County, so owners there deal with Limestone County offices. Call them for their dates, since the figures here are from Madison County.

Payment methodFee or rule
Credit or debit card2.75 percent fee plus $0.30
E-check$1.50 fee
Personal checkNot accepted in April or May

The county sends a courtesy notice by October 1, but Alabama law does not require a bill before taxes become delinquent, so a new owner should look up the bill online. The bill follows the owner of record on October 1 of the prior year.

If a seller leaves a tax balance unpaid after closing, the buyer inherits the problem. For that reason the closing office normally pays it from your proceeds. Ask it to prorate the year's bill, and keep the receipt.

For Madison County parcels the deed goes to the probate office at the Madison County Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW in Huntsville. The county tells new owners to verify the recording, then assess the property and claim exemptions.

Alabama's recording tax is 50 cents for every $500 of value, with proof of the price attached, as Alabama Code 40-22-1 provides.

Madison grew around a railroad stop and was incorporated on December 2, 1869. In 1986, voters chose to stay independent rather than merge with Huntsville, and the city then expanded rapidly. The Madison Historic District joined the National Register of Historic Places in 2006. If your house is in or near it, mention that to buyers.

sections.h2: Selling in a market full of similar houses
sections.html:
Because so much of Madison was built within a few decades, buyers see rows of houses with similar floor plans. What separates yours is the small stuff: the age of the roof and the heating and cooling, the condition of the kitchen and baths, and whether the yard drains. List each one plainly.

Price against what is for sale now, not what sold years ago. If a house has tenant trouble, deferred repairs or an unfinished renovation, a financed buyer will often pass, and that is where a cash purchase can fit.

Owners who are relocating for a job on the Redstone side of the metro often have a closing date they cannot move. In that case, tell any buyer your deadline at the start, so the contract works from your date backward.

sections.h2: Selling a Madison house for cash
sections.html:
A cash sale suits owners who want to skip showings and buyer financing. In a city with many fairly new homes, the common reasons to sell fast are relocation, divorce, inheritance and tenant trouble.

  • Confirm the county, Madison or Limestone, for the parcel.
  • Check the October 1 tax status.
  • Ask for a title search.
  • Gather HOA documents if there are any.

sections.h2: Selling a house in a Madison HOA
sections.html:
Many Madison subdivisions have a homeowners association. Before you list, ask the association for its governing documents, current dues and any special assessment, and find out whether it requires a payoff letter at closing. A buyer will ask for all of it, and the closing office cannot finish the file without it.

If your yard, fence or exterior was changed, check that the association approved the work. An unapproved change can delay closing or be raised by the buyer's inspector.

sections.h2: Selling with tenants or an inherited house
sections.html: A rented house can be sold with the lease in place, so read the lease for notice terms. For an inherited house, the court papers must show who is allowed to sign before a deed can pass. Start with the deed, the newest tax bill and any lender statement, and a title search will show what else needs clearing.

After you accept an offer, a title search checks for liens, unpaid tax and ownership questions. A lender with an open mortgage supplies a payoff figure. At closing you sign the deed and the settlement statement, the payoff and tax split are handled, and the deed goes to the probate office of the county where the parcel lies.

Bring a photo ID and every key and garage opener. If the house sits in an HOA, ask the association for its documents and any dues owed, since a closing office may need a payoff letter from it.

faqs.q: What is the population of Madison, AL?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 67,968 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 56,933.

faqs.q: Is Madison, AL in Madison County or Limestone County?
faqs.a: Mostly Madison County, with a western portion in Limestone County.

faqs.q: What is the Madison County tax rate inside Madison city?
faqs.a: It is $6.95 per $100 of assessed value for property inside the city of Madison.

faqs.q: When are Madison property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: After December 31. Taxes are due October 1, and a $5 late fee plus 1 percent monthly interest follow.
No. Madison is a separate city that Huntsville surrounds. Voters chose independence in 1986.
